articles.title: Voice Labs experiments with commands shaped around each home
articles.dek: The English-only experiment lets households define commands and give the same words different meanings by room.
body: Voice Labs experiments with voice commands shaped around the people and rooms in a home. Households can define phrases that run a script, activate a scene, carry out an action or speak a response. Commands can apply throughout the home or only in one room, so the same words can do something different depending on which satellite hears them.

The project is experimental and unsupported, and currently hears and speaks English. Trying it requires a Home Assistant app, a custom integration installed through HACS and alternate firmware for Voice Preview Edition satellites. Michael Hansen makes his first contribution to the experimental-apps repository with the addition.

Command matching runs on the Home Assistant host, but the speech-engine settings determine where other audio processing happens. If Home Assistant Cloud is signed in and no engine has been chosen, the app initially selects its speech recognition and voice, streaming every command as it is spoken. Owners can instead choose the app’s built-in models and keep that processing local.

pullRequests.title: Add Voice Labs

articles.title: Change connection settings without rebuilding your integrations
articles.dek: Cameras, speakers and other connected services gain a way to update an existing setup.
body: Changing a device address or an account setting does not have to mean deleting its Home Assistant integration and starting again. A broad set of integrations gains reconfiguration, covering connections such as ONVIF cameras, Harmony hubs, Roomba vacuums and Tesla Wall Connectors.

The available settings match each integration: some let you change the host address, while others also accept connection options or credentials. Where supported, a device identity check prevents accidentally replacing the original device with a different one. Existing pairing details are reused for connections such as IKEA TRÅDFRI and Lutron Caséta.

Cloud accounts get their own routes through the same process. August, Netatmo and ViCare support starting authentication again manually; Seafile accepts changed connection and account details. The options differ by service rather than exposing one identical form everywhere.

articles.title: ESPHome 2026.10.2 protects Realtek devices during wireless updates
articles.dek: A safer first upgrade avoids a compression fault that could leave an RTL8710B device unable to start.
body: ESPHome 2026.10.2 fixes a wireless-update fault that could leave devices using the RTL8710B chip unable to start. Introduced in 2026.10.0, the problem could corrupt a compressed upload and still select the damaged firmware at restart, requiring a serial cable to recover the device.

Owners should update the ESPHome upload tool before updating affected devices. J. Nick Koston’s correction makes that tool send the first update to affected firmware without compression. The transfer takes longer, but later updates can use compression again after the corrected firmware is installed.

The correction also keeps refused or interrupted uploads from becoming the next boot image on LibreTiny devices. Hardware checks on RTL8710B, RTL8720C, BK7238 and LN882H boards confirmed that failed image checks and interrupted uploads preserved the running firmware.

pullRequests.title: [ota] Work around the LibreTiny OTA issue that bricks RTL8710B on a compressed update

articles.title: Calibrate sensor readings with a visual setup
articles.dek: Compensation turns pairs of measured and reference values into a corrected sensor.
body: Home Assistant’s Compensation integration gains a visual setup for creating a corrected sensor from an existing reading. Pick the source sensor, then enter pairs of measured values and the values they should represent, instead of defining the calibration in YAML.

The helper can fit a straight line or a curve through those reference points. Its options include rounding, units and lower or upper limits, so the result can match the scale you need. It produces a separate corrected sensor; it does not change the physical device’s calibration.

articles.title: Assist stops falling behind a busy Android dashboard
articles.dek: A voice-audio change keeps older phones from accumulating speech while the screen is busy.
body: A busy dashboard can leave an older Android device sending speech to Assist long after it was recorded. The Companion app moves that audio work away from the screen’s main thread and sends queued audio together, preventing a slow interface from steadily pushing the conversation behind.

Timothy tested the change on a OnePlus 3 while its dashboard was busy. The observed start of voice activity fell from about 1.7 seconds to 0.6 seconds, and an audio backlog that previously grew to around 800 milliseconds no longer accumulated. Those figures describe that test, rather than a promised speedup for every phone.
The app also discards remaining audio when speech recognition finishes, so a completed request does not continue sending old sound.

pullRequests.title: Try to improve wake word use case on slow device

articles.title: Music Assistant creates covers for playlists without artwork
articles.dek: Connected image engines provide six styles or a custom prompt, with generation limits and a collage fallback.
body: Music Assistant’s Playlist Metadata provider adds an AI-generated cover option for playlists that do not already have their own artwork. Ryan Macdonald connects it to an image engine supplied through a Home Assistant AI Task entity or the OpenAI Compatible plugin, with six built-in styles and a custom prompt option.

Covers are saved and reused until relevant playlist or generation settings change. A configurable hourly limit caps generation, a preview tries a style without changing a playlist, and a collage remains in place while an image is prepared or if none is produced.
A separate option writes short playlist descriptions. It starts disabled and does not replace an ordinary description supplied by the playlist’s owner.

pullRequests.title: Add AI generated covers and descriptions to the Playlist Metadata provider
Document the AI generated covers and descriptions of Playlist Metadata

media.alt: Three example generated playlist covers titled Chill Vibes, Club Heat and Indie Singalongs.

articles.title: Music Assistant continues listening with a similar artist
articles.dek: A new Autoplay mode follows the chosen artist playback order instead of adding loose tracks.
body: Music Assistant adds a Similar artists Autoplay mode. When the queue runs low, it chooses an artist related to the last track’s artist and adds music using the listener’s configured way of playing an artist.

With an album-based order and shuffle off, that means whole albums one after another. The mode leaves the queue’s shuffle setting unchanged, skips artists already represented in the queue and leaves out disliked tracks. It adds nothing when there are no similar artists left, and is unavailable when no connected provider supplies them.

pullRequests.title: Add a similar artists Autoplay mode
Document the similar artists Autoplay option
Note that similar artists Autoplay keeps the queue's shuffle

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps restricted accounts within their assigned players
articles.dek: Queue commands and shared-account requests follow the listener’s own source and player permissions.
body: Music Assistant applies a listener’s player restrictions throughout its queue controls. An account limited to selected players could previously read and change other players’ queues; the checks now cover queue commands, including both players when transferring a queue.

Fabian Munkes also carries a listener’s identity through item reads, recommendations, playlist changes and lyrics requests made on their behalf. Those requests use the listener’s permitted music sources, while automatic queue refills run as the queue owner.

pullRequests.title: Allow impersonation on playlist edits, queue commands and lyrics
Allow impersonation on item reads and recommendations

articles.title: Z-Wave JS blocks unwanted device replacement requests
articles.dek: Stricter checks prevent an ordinary node from triggering a replacement that strips another device’s security permissions.
body: Z-Wave JS rejects device-replacement requests from ordinary nodes. Such a request could previously remove and recreate an existing device, then leave its security permissions unset when the attempted setup failed.

The driver now accepts these requests only from a known controller while it is idle, and refuses requests targeting the controller itself or the sender. It also avoids adding an already known device through proxy inclusion unless that device has just announced itself as part of the same pairing process.

articles.title: The Android app raises its minimum to Android 7
articles.dek: Android 6 devices fall outside the supported range for future app builds.
body: Future Home Assistant Companion builds require Android 7 or newer, raising the minimum from Android 6. The change matters for older phones and tablets still serving as wall panels: those devices will need a newer operating system or replacement hardware to keep following app updates.
The new minimum follows the requirements of Android’s supporting libraries.

articles.title: Zonneplan prices follow quarter-hour electricity contracts
articles.dek: A dedicated price sensor matches 15-minute billing while hourly prices remain available.
body: Zonneplan customers billed in 15-minute blocks gain a matching electricity-price sensor in Home Assistant. It uses the quarter-hour prices supplied by Zonneplan rather than the hourly average, giving price-based automations the same time scale as those contracts.

The existing hourly price sensor stays in place. A companion correction updates its value at the start of the hour from prices already fetched, avoiding a wait for the next periodic refresh without adding more requests to Zonneplan.

Fix Zonneplan price sensors lagging behind after the hour
Add Zonneplan quarter-hour electricity price

articles.title: Control Omada VPN policies from Home Assistant
articles.dek: Existing VPN connections gain switches that dashboards and automations can use.
body: Home Assistant gains switches for VPN policies already configured on TP-Link Omada gateways. Each policy has its own switch, allowing a dashboard or automation to enable or disable it without opening the Omada controller.

The connection covers server, client and site-to-site VPN policies and attaches the switches to the gateway device. It controls existing policies rather than creating a VPN configuration; controllers with no supported policies expose no switches.

articles.title: Axis Companion cameras regain video and device events
articles.dek: A model-specific connection setting restores cameras that otherwise reject their streams.
body: Axis Companion cameras get a connection adjustment for video and event streams that their firmware otherwise rejects. Home Assistant detects the Companion models and applies the required camera option, addressing unavailable cameras and missing event-driven entities.

Richard Huish checked live video, infrared lighting and events including motion, sound and passive-infrared detection on Companion Cube L and Cube LW cameras running firmware 9.80.132. The adjustment applies specifically to Companion models.

articles.title: Z-Wave JS adds Zooz fixes for missed heat and false CO alerts
articles.dek: Two firmware catalogue additions address specific alarm-reporting faults.
body: Z-Wave JS’s firmware catalogue adds Zooz ZSE44-V02 firmware 2.50.0 for US and European devices. It corrects a fault where the high-temperature alert did not trigger with Celsius selected even though normal temperature readings continued.

The catalogue also adds US ZEN55 firmware 1.60.0. Its correction targets false carbon-monoxide alerts when the ZEN55 is connected to a Kidde 30CUAR-VRF detector that is wirelessly interconnected with another Kidde detector using Kidde RF.

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps SoundCloud signed in
articles.dek: An optional refresh-token setting avoids repeatedly pasting a new token after it expires.
body: Music Assistant renews SoundCloud access tokens before they expire, or at startup if they have already expired. SoundCloud’s newer sign-in tokens can expire within a day, leaving the provider unable to connect until the owner pastes another one.
Rob Sonke adds an optional refresh-token setting and saves replacement tokens as soon as SoundCloud rotates them. The existing sign-in method for older tokens stays unchanged.

roadmapUpdates.summary: Paul Bottein says the direction for Home Assistant’s redesigned cover controls is clear, but he is checking it against devices without position or stop controls, unknown states and other capabilities before proposing adjustments.
